actions.body: Systemic failure in intelligent agents often emerges not from a lack of capacity, but from the rigidity of programmed objectives in dynamic environments. As analyzed in recent literature, the transition from planning to action introduces a critical bottleneck. Specifically, the literature notes the tension between goal formulation and the actualization of a strategy: 'versus to the execution of a solution plan. Recent research on rational agency has highlighted the importance o' (source-e8ebac5ba0244992). This gap between plan formulation and real-world application acts as a latency that permits utility function drift when environmental variables change faster than the agent's metareasoning cycle (source-c6430c5161404598).
actions.lede: Exploring the structural failures of rigid objective-following through the lens of rational agency constraints.
